newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China Grains - Soybean, meal, seen out of reach.
newsitem.headline: China Grains - Soybean, meal, seen out of reach.

text.p: China's grains markets were quiet as prices edged above what Chinese buyers were willing to pay, grains and oilseeds traders said on Thursday.
"The prices are too high. China cannot accept these levels," said one source.
The domestic price of soybean meal was around 2,750 yuan ($331) per tonne, which made imported meal more than 200 yuan more expensive than local meal.

One grains source said he knew of a Chinese feed mill that had bought about 250,000 tonnes of South American soymeal over the course of January and February, priced at about $280 per tonne, C&F China, for shipment in May.
"They bought it in small amounts at a time," the grains source said, noting that 250,000 tonnes was not a significant amount.
This could not be confirmed.
Chicago Board of Trade (CBOT) soymeal ended higher on Wednesday, partially supported by talk that China had bought Argentine meal, with May up $4.70 at $274.20 per tonne.
Other Hong Kong and China-based traders said that Chinese end users had been playing a waiting game, anticipating bean and meal prices would drop. The market climbed instead.
"I've been urging my (Chinese) clients to buy now before prices go higher," said one trader, noting he hoped the mindset of Chinese buyers would re-adjust to accept firmer prices.
Meal demand remained strong, traders said.
Some traders noted that Chinese buyers were not put off by high prices themselves, since feed meal demand was healthy.
"It's the price erosion they're afraid of," one source said, noting that Chinese customers were afraid to get their fingers burnt if they bought at current levels and prices dropped.
CBOT soybeans rallied on Wednesday to close higher on unconfirmed rumours that China bought about 50,000 tonnes of U.S. soybeans for prompt shipment.
About 10,000 tonnes of corn was heard sold to a Southeast Asian destination over the last week, but no details were available.
About 50,000 tonnes of U.S. dehulled soybeans was heard obtained by a mill in southwestern China.
